title: Add downgrade guard, safe rollback tooling, and version-pinned backup/restore for private-installer (Helm/Terraform)
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds guarded upgrade/rollback flow for Private Installer: pinned module/chart versions, preflight backup/restore tools, schema migration with version table, and downgrade guard to prevent accidental rollbacks. No breaking API changes; operators should run the included preflight before upgrading.
description:
Context: During recent Private Installer upgrades we observed a failure mode where downstream schema migrations could not be safely rolled back, producing partial upgrades requiring manual intervention (see ENG-3482). This PR implements three coordinated pieces to make upgrades and rollbacks safe: 1) explicit version pinning for Helm charts and Terraform modules so the upgrade plan is reproducible; 2) preflight backup + restore tooling with automated verification; 3) a lightweight migration version table + downgrade guard that prevents applying a lower cluster version unless an explicit --force-downgrade flag is provided and offline backup exists.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds /scripts/backup_restore.sh and a python preflight script that verifies backups before upgrade and validates post-restore invariants.
- Pins chart images and module versions in charts/private-installer/values.yaml and terraform/modules/installer/main.tf.
- Adds a migration to create cluster_version table and writes current installer version during upgrades.
- Implements a Terraform pre-apply check (installer/terraform/upgrade_guard.tf) that reads cluster_version and errors out on safe-downgrade attempts.
- Adds a Helm post-install hook that creates an on-cluster snapshot marker for operator visibility.
- Adds documentation and a runnable example in docs/upgrade-guide.md.

Checklist: 
- [x] Backup script + verification unit tests
- [x] Migration SQL + idempotent semantics
- [x] Helm & Terraform changes linted
- [x] Integration smoke tests for upgrade/rollback
- [x] Docs updated and release notes written

Operational notes: Run ./installer/scripts/preflight_check.py --backup before applying release/v1.8. The preflight exits non-zero on missing backups or incompatible schema diffs. To intentionally downgrade, use --force-downgrade and follow the documented restore procedure (docs/upgrade-guide.md).

Related: ENG-3482, ENG-3490, SUP-1263

review_comments: Ben Carlson (review): Nice work, Priya. Two asks: (1) can the preflight detect active request load to avoid upgrading hot clusters? (2) ensure migrations are idempotent if applied twice. See inline comments.

Priya Natarajan (author reply): Added a simple traffic-check in preflight_check.py (returns non-zero if active_connections > 1000). Migration SQL was rewritten to use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + UPSERT semantics to be idempotent.

Marta Ivanov (review): Terraform guard looks good but prefer failing-fast in plan, not apply. Updated guard to run during terraform plan via an external data source. Please add unit tests for the data source behaviour.
Priya Natarajan (author reply): Moved the guard to plan-time using an external data source and added test in terraform/tests/guard_test.sh
Darnell Brooks (approval): Verified end-to-end on a staging cluster and tested forced downgrade flow with documented restore. Approving. CI green after final lint fix.
